elements.element: Customer is not subject to any employee non-solicitation restriction.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause expressly provides that “neither party will solicit,” so it binds Customer.

elements.element: The non-solicitation restriction applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: The restriction applies to “neither party” soliciting employees of “the other party.”

elements.element: The restriction is limited to personnel directly involved in the services under the Agreement.
elements.evidence: It covers only an employee “who is directly involved in performing services under this Agreement.”

elements.element: For each covered person, the restriction lasts only through twelve months after the end of that person's involvement in the services.
elements.evidence: The clause applies “During the Term” as well as for twelve months after the person's involvement ends. If involvement ends more than twelve months before the Term ends, the restriction could continue for the remainder of the Term. In addition, the present-tense phrase “who is directly involved” creates uncertainty about whether former participants remain covered during the intended post-involvement period.

elements.element: General job advertisements are excluded from solicitation.
elements.evidence: The definition expressly excludes “generally advertising job openings” and follow-up with individuals responding to those advertisements.

elements.element: Unsolicited approaches or employment inquiries initiated by an individual are excluded from solicitation.
elements.evidence: The definition excludes follow-up with individuals “who voluntarily initiate employment inquiries.”

elements.element: The clause does not prohibit hiring personnel where no prohibited solicitation occurred.
elements.evidence: The operative prohibition addresses only solicitation, defined as affirmative targeted recruitment; it contains no separate no-hire restriction.

result.reason: The redline does not achieve the preferred position because Customer remains bound. It substantially tracks the fallback, but the retained “During the Term” language can extend the restriction beyond twelve months after an individual's involvement ends. The present-tense eligibility language also conflicts with or obscures the intended post-involvement tail. Removing the agreement-wide Term trigger and tying coverage clearly to persons who are or were directly involved would be necessary to satisfy the fallback.
